summary: Iteration 4 validated the localStorage->httpOnly cookie auth migration end-to-end. Backend: added 7 new pytest cases (TestCookieAuth) covering login-sets-httpOnly-cookie, /auth/me via cookie, logout clears cookie, admin cookie authorizes PUT /admin/content, member cookie rejected by admin route, Bearer fallback still works, guest checkout no-cookie, and logged-in checkout with cookie. Also refactored the pytest scaffolding: shared session `s` is now a NoCookieSession that clears cookies on every response, and admin_token/member_token fixtures use one-shot requests calls so login cookies don't leak into the Bearer-based regression suite. Result: 45/45 pytest cases pass (was 29/38 with cookie leakage). Frontend browser flow: anon /admin & /portal both redirect to /login; admin login lands on /admin, sets httpOnly access_token cookie (Secure, SameSite=None, Partitioned via Emergent proxy — expected), localStorage contains ONLY posthog telemetry (no auth token); hard page reload keeps admin on /admin (cookie session persists); admin CMS PUT /api/admin/content/home returns 200 while authenticated only by cookie; 'Sign out' button posts /api/auth/logout and clears cookie — /api/auth/me then returns 401 and /admin redirects to /login; member login lands on /portal, hard reload persists, member visiting /admin gets bounced back to /portal (role gating works).
critical_code_review_comments: get_current_user() prefers the cookie over the Authorization header. This is fine for browser flows but means that if a client sends BOTH (e.g., a stale cookie plus a Bearer for a different user), the cookie silently wins — the previous pytest suite hit exactly this edge case because a shared requests.Session accumulated login cookies. Consider a small doc comment on set_auth_cookie/get_current_user or reversing precedence (Bearer > cookie) so API-first clients cannot be silently overridden by a stale cookie.

set_auth_cookie uses samesite='lax' and secure=True. The Emergent proxy rewrites this to SameSite=None; Secure; Partitioned (verified in the browser). The literal 'lax' value therefore has no effect on the deployed cookie — consider setting samesite='none' explicitly in code so local/dev environments match production.

AuthContext initial /auth/me on mount ALWAYS 401s for anonymous visitors, which spams the browser console with 'Failed to load resource: 401'. Consider suppressing the axios error log for /auth/me or making the endpoint return 200 with {authenticated: false} to avoid noisy console errors on every anonymous page load.

server.py has crossed 850 lines and still lives as a single module; the cookie migration is a good moment to split into routers (auth, shows, payments, admin) — flagged in iteration 3 as well and still outstanding.
seed_data_creation: All 4 seeded shows are status=past (no active/upcoming show), so the UI booking box on ShowDetail always shows 'This season has closed.' and does NOT render buyer-name/buyer-email/checkout-btn. Guest+authenticated checkout paths are still fully verified via pytest (TestCookieAuth.test_guest_checkout_no_cookie, test_logged_in_checkout_uses_cookie_user, TestGuestCheckoutMarketing). If UI-driven checkout needs to be exercised, create an upcoming show via POST /api/admin/shows and clean up afterwards.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Auth is now httpOnly-cookie based (access_token) with Bearer fallback in get_current_user. The pytest suite at /app/backend/tests/backend_test.py has a NoCookieSession `s` fixture that discards cookies after every response — DO NOT replace it with a plain requests.Session or Bearer-vs-cookie precedence bugs will re-appear. New TestCookieAuth class documents the expected cookie flow. Logout button in the admin/portal shell has text 'Sign out' (not 'Logout'). All 4 seeded shows remain status=past. Emergent proxy rewrites cookie to SameSite=None; Secure; Partitioned — expected and correct.
rca of the issue: N/A — migration validated cleanly. The initial pytest failures were caused by the shared requests.Session in the pre-migration test file: after cookie auth was enabled, logging in with admin (then member) via the same Session left an admin cookie in the jar, and get_current_user's cookie-first precedence caused member Bearer tokens and even anon requests to be silently upgraded to the admin identity — surfacing as false 200s where 401/403 were expected. Fix: refactor test fixtures to isolate cookies from the shared session; no backend code change needed.
